title: Waves
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 9 Integrated Science; not yet checked by a CBC Integrated Science teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: A rope shaken up and down for transverse waves, a slinky spring pushed and pulled for longitudinal waves, a basin of water with a dropped stone. Remote sensing is taught with weather satellite pictures and the radio and phone signals learners use.

skills.key_step: The child says waves are made by vibrations and carry energy, not matter, and tells transverse waves (particles move at right angles to the direction of travel: water, light) from longitudinal waves (particles move back and forth along it: sound).
representations: a rope shaken up and down
a floating leaf on a basin of water
steps: The wave carries energy; the matter stays.
Transverse: up and down while the wave goes along.
Longitudinal: back and forth along the direction (squeezes and stretches).

board.do: Draw a rope with an up-and-down wave and an arrow showing travel.
Point at one bit of rope.
board.say: Which way does this bit move as the wave passes?

board.do: Ask how the coils of a slinky move for sound.

misconceptions.ask: Which way did the slinky coils move?
Which way did the floating leaf move?

listen_for: particles move along with the wave
misconceptions.ask: Did the bit of rope travel along?
misconceptions.repair: Transverse particles move at right angles.

listen_for: the water goes to the edge
misconceptions.ask: Did the leaf reach the edge?
misconceptions.repair: A wave carries energy, not water.

checks.question: Is sound a transverse or a longitudinal wave?
What does a wave carry from place to place?

skills.key_step: The child names the features of a wave (crest, trough, amplitude, wavelength, frequency in hertz, speed), and describes remote sensing and other uses of waves (radio, phones, satellites, X-rays, ultrasound).

floor.prerequisite: Can tell transverse from longitudinal waves.
floor.question: Which kind is a water wave?

representations: a rope shaken slowly and quickly
steps: Amplitude: height from the middle line.
Wavelength: crest to crest (metres); frequency: waves per second (hertz).
Uses: radio, phones, remote sensing by satellites, ultrasound scans.
contexts: a weather forecast from satellite pictures
an ultrasound scan at a clinic

board.do: Draw a wave with two crests.
Point at the distance between two crests.
Ask the child to mark the amplitude.

misconceptions.ask: What is a cattle trough like: high or low?
Is amplitude a height or a length along?
misconceptions.repair: Crest to crest is the wavelength.

misconceptions.ask: Did the big and small shakes arrive together?
misconceptions.repair: Amplitude does not change the speed.

checks.question: What is the unit of frequency?
Give one use of waves in remote sensing.
checks.answer: satellites taking pictures for weather forecasts or mapping crops
